title: C
subtitle: The small, fast language underneath operating systems, databases and language runtimes, taught as modern C17 with an eye on C23.
description: C is a small, compiled language created at Bell Labs in the early 1970s to write the Unix operating system, and it still sits underneath much of computing: the Linux kernel, embedded firmware, SQLite and PostgreSQL, the interpreters of Python, Ruby and Lua, Git and curl. It gives you direct control over memory and very little protection from mistakes, which is why it is both fast and famously unforgiving. Its calling conventions and data layouts are also the common language through which almost every other language talks to the operating system and to each other.

This course teaches **modern C**: the C17 standard, with notes on what C23 adds and which compilers support it. It goes from compiling a first program, through types, pointers, strings, structs and dynamic memory, to the preprocessor, the standard library, undefined behaviour, sanitizers, testing and build tools, and ends with a hash-table project. It assumes the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience: you know what a variable, a loop and a function are. No previous C is needed.

To run the programs you need a C compiler. On Linux install GCC or Clang from your distribution (`sudo apt install build-essential` on Debian and Ubuntu); on macOS run `xcode-select --install` for Apple's Clang; on Windows use Visual Studio's C/C++ tools, MSYS2's GCC, or a Linux distribution under WSL. C has no official online playground, because it is an ISO standard rather than a single project, but [Compiler Explorer](https://godbolt.org/) can compile and run C in the browser with many versions of GCC and Clang.

levels.title: The core language
levels.summary: Compiling and running C, its types and operators, control flow and functions, and the pointers and arrays that everything else is built on.

levels.title: Text, data and memory
levels.summary: Strings as arrays of bytes, structs, enums and unions for modelling data, and dynamic memory with the bugs it invites and the sanitizers that catch them.

levels.title: C as professionals write it
levels.summary: Headers, the preprocessor and the standard library, undefined behaviour and how to test against it, and make and CMake builds for a complete hash-table project.
